old: Why this verdict and not another. Three candidate readings were put up before the pages were read, and each was tested against what the vendor wrote rather than against its marketing headline. (1) The address is a real rung-5 move: an ISP-registered prefix in a non-Cloudflare ASN. Supported, and the vendor says so twice, once on the product page as Registered to real internet providers, not hosting companies. (2) It is a datacenter box wearing a residential ASN, so any upstream that keys on the hosting environment rather than the ASN still sees a datacenter address. Also supported, and conceded by the vendor in the help article. That second reading is why the verdict carries a caveat: the purchase buys one of the two signals, and the topic cannot yet say which signal the refusing upstream uses. (3) The 250 GB allowance makes it unusable. Refuted at this scale, because the gateway moves on the order of 45 GB a month, so 250 GB is about 5.5 times the month and not a quarter of it. The rung-5 question is what a purchase would settle, and it is the only one of the three that is still open. What would settle it: buy the 20-address plan at $6.00, take one address, echo it from ip.pkgforge.dev, resolve its ASN with RIPE prefix-overview, look it up in a hosting database, then send the same request the upstream refuses to that address and from a Cloudflare address in the same minute. Until then the split is the vendor's account of its own product and nothing more. Every claim here rests on one read of each of three pages on one day; there is no second sample. This record CORRECTS dossier/debrid/webshare.json, which files the same provider under the wrong topic for the wrong question: that record prices it as an egress path and judges the 250 GB against a 1 TiB storage month, so it reads the allowance as a quarter of the month and reaches the same verdict for the wrong reason. Webshare sells an address, the unit here is cost per distinct address-class, and against the gateway's 45 GB the allowance is headroom rather than the binding failure. Two records now describe one provider; the debrid one should be retired to history/ once the ip-proxy document exists. One structural note for a later session: the schema's interface enum has no value for a proxy protocol, so socks5 and http-proxy cannot be recorded as tokens and the protocols live in interface_detail. That is a schema gap this new topic will hit on every record, and it is worth adding the two tokens rather than repeating this note.
new: Paid-only: the Static Residential (ISP) product has no free tier, trial or recurring credit, and the account’s free plan is a separate datacenter offer. A purchase buys an address whose ASN is a residential ISP, not a residential hosting environment: the vendor states that the IP address belongs to a residential ISP while the server it runs on sits in a datacenter, so a check of the ASN shows a residential ISP such as AT&T or Comcast, and a check of the hosting environment may show datacenter or hosting. Which of the two signals a refusing upstream reads is unverified without a bought address. The same provider is also filed as debrid/webshare, priced there as an egress path. The interface vocabulary has no token for an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy endpoint, so the protocols are recorded in interface_detail.
